Here's the full picture, including answers to your three asks:

## Where everything stands

**Merged today:** #1134 (OTP backend core — after I cleared the CodeQL false-positive blocking it), **#1140** (shared circuit breaker, closes #1135), **#1143** (SMTP pre-flight, closes #737). Issues #734, #735, #1127, #1135, #737 all verified individually closed.

**Auto-merge armed, landing as CI goes green:**
- **#1148** — the big one: frontend `otp` mode (two-step sign-in, HttpOnly-cookie session, 11-spec fully-local OTP E2E lane in CI) **plus the #1138 nginx `X-Forwarded-Proto` fix**. The 5-agent review came back clean except one docstring overclaim, already fixed. Closes #736 + #1138 on merge.
- **#1144** — test-DB isolation (#1130 + #1133); review found two latent test-integrity gaps (vacuous-lock risk, E2E opt-in narrowed to one env var) — both fixed, E2E now gated on an explicit `DATAQ_E2E=1`.
- **#1145** — OTP purge beat wiring (#1136); review caught a real one (scored 95): no `<=0` guard meant a misconfigured retention value would have instantly deleted **live** sign-in codes. Guard + test added, sibling-sweep pattern.
- **#1142** — the #1137 constant-time floor (1.0s, monotonic-clock remainder, errors deliberately unpadded); reviewed clean, one missing env-table row being added now, then I arm it.

**Still running:** the **#1128** agent (/mcp + PATs in otp-only mode — resumed after the session-limit kill). Queued after the wave: **#1139** (display-name profile completion), the batched `docs/progress.md` update, and **#1141**/**#1147**/**#1146** (filed findings: verify-side timing channel, admin-endpoint mail throttle, mailer CA-bundle option).

## Your two design questions

**Our own mailbox — no for production, yes for local.** Bundling a real outbound mailer in a self-hosted product is a deliverability trap: direct-to-MX from an arbitrary self-hosted IP with no SPF/DKIM/rDNS reputation gets spam-foldered or rejected — precisely on the sign-in critical path — and shipping an open relay inside the appliance is an abuse liability. A vendor-hosted relay would route your users' sign-in metadata through a third party, against the self-hosted posture. Where we *can* remove the setup burden is local/eval: bundle a local inbox (MailHog-style; the #736 E2E lane already built the harder TLS-capable version) so codes land in a web inbox at `localhost:8025` with zero SMTP configuration.

**OTP as the local default — yes for the eval stack, keep bypass for the dev loop.** This is the same lesson as the OpenBao flip: the eval stack's defaults are the security posture evaluators actually run, and bypass-by-default means anyone on the host is admin. Proposal: the published eval compose defaults to `otp` + the bundled inbox, with `setup.sh` prompting your email into the allowlist (fail-closed stays intact — empty allowlist still refuses to boot); contributors' dev loop and the CI bypass lane stay as-is. Both halves are captured in **[#1150](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1150)** — say the word and I'll build it once #1148 is in.

I'll report back as the merge wave and #1128 complete.

- `_PatOrJwtVerifier` now takes `JWTVerifier | None`. In `pat_only` the JWT half is **genuinely absent**, not an unconfigured validator: a non-PAT bearer hits `if self._jwt is None: return None` → fastmcp's uniform 401, having reached no validator at all. An unconfigured verifier never becomes an accept-anything path, and no token material is handed to something that logs what it can't decode (#849).
- `dq_sess_` stays rejected **by prefix, first**, in every mode. The cookie still never authenticates `/mcp` (bearer-only; the "cookies never appear in mcp/auth.py" structural test still passes).

71 tests in `backend/tests/mcp/`; full local battery green — black, ruff, mypy (326 files), bandit (no issues), `pre-commit` incl. betterleaks, and **3511 passed / 1 skipped, coverage 97.05%** against scratch DB `dataq_test_1128`. All three now go through one new `RangeReader`/`read_range` seam: Parquet answers schema *and* `num_rows` from its footer in a couple of small range GETs whatever the object's size, and CSV takes a bounded head read for its schema and a **streamed** pyarrow scan for its count. A run mixing volume with column-freshness still reads the object exactly once. (**2026-07-25 (later still) — #943 shipped, closing the unbounded-flat-file class.** Batch resolution drained every page under the prefix into a list on **every run**, before the runner was even built — so a landing zone with a long history of dated files grew the retained listing without bound on a scheduled path. The listing is now streamed and folded in a single pass keeping only the running bests, so memory is flat regardless of history. The fold reproduces the previous `max()` calls *exactly*, including their first-wins tie-breaking — pinned by a parametrised equivalence test that recomputes the original formulation, because a `>=` would silently flip every tie. **AC 1 as written ('read a bounded number of pages') was not implementable safely and was deliberately not faked:** both stores list ascending, so the newest key — the one `latest` wants — is precisely what a truncated scan misses, and a capped scan would return a confidently wrong older batch. Instead a generous hard limit *refuses* (`BatchListingTooLargeError`, deliberately not a `BatchNotFoundError`, which would skip the run and report success nightly) and a soft limit logs so the cost is visible before it is an incident. The retention test needed two attempts: the first measured *after* the fold returned, where every local is already dead, so it passed against a full materialisation — it now samples peak retention mid-stream. | ✅ | **#737 SMTP pre-flight** — `POST /admin/auth-email/test` (admin-gated, caller's-own-address-only so it structurally can't relay), `_deliver()` stage ladder shared with `send_code`, stage-typed 502s (`connect/tls/auth/send`), redaction proven through the real logging pipeline, Admin-UI "Send test email" button, runbook smoke step. The `/code-review` flow caught a real regression pre-merge: the refactor left the `with smtp` statement unguarded, so a real `smtplib.__exit__` `SMTPResponseException` on QUIT would **replace** the in-flight stage error and escape as a raw 500 on the production sign-in path — the PR's SMTP fakes structurally couldn't see it (never-raising `__exit__`); fixed with an explicit `quit()`-in-`finally` + regression tests. Review also filed [#1147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1147) (no mailer-appropriate throttle on the endpoint — generic 300/min token class vs the 10/min auth class) | [#1143](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1143) merged 2026-08-02 |
| ✅ | **#1128 `/mcp` in otp-only** — one `mcp_auth_mode()` ladder (`azure_ad → pat_only → dev_bypass → disabled`) mirroring `core.auth`'s exactly (the old gate + log line each re-derived the mode, which is how otp-only ended up unmounted AND mislabeled `dev_bypass`). In `pat_only` the JWT half of `_PatOrJwtVerifier` is genuinely `None` — a non-PAT bearer reaches **no validator** (uniform 401, #849-safe); `dq_sess_` stays rejected by prefix first in every mode; OTP now outranks dev-bypass (a tightening, and it removes a REST-vs-MCP mode disagreement). The OTP-user journey is pinned end-to-end: cookie session mints a PAT via `/me/api-keys` → PAT authenticates all 8 tools on `/mcp`. Each fix half was revert-tested (5/9/4 tests fail respectively); one test was caught passing for the wrong reason (rescued by the suite-wide `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`) and re-pinned | [#1151](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1151) merged 2026-08-02 |
| ✅ | **Findings batch** — every #1134-review finding fixed same-track: **#1135** shared `CircuitBreaker` (one mechanism, per-store state so an OTP brownout can't disable rate limiting; the extraction preserved every #1016 lesson, and the review's one finding — the new monotonic-clock contract vs `rate_limit`'s wall-clock `_now` — was fixed with a dedicated monotonic breaker clock + a discriminating test) → [#1140](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1140); **#1137** constant-time floor on `otp/request` (`AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_MIN_SECONDS`, default 1.0s, monotonic remainder-sleep, errors deliberately unpadded, docs re-scoped to name the SMTP-tail residual; the narrower verify-side channel filed as [#1141](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1141)) → [#1142](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1142); **#1130 + #1133** test-DB isolation (conftest redirects `DATABASE_URL`→`TEST_DATABASE_URL` **before** the engine-building imports — the naive after-import fix was empirically a no-op; lock-test fixtures rebound to the test engine + User-row teardown; review then hardened both its own gaps: visible-row assertions so the lock tests can't go vacuous under URL divergence, and an explicit `DATAQ_E2E=1` opt-in after the redirect silently narrowed the real-infra E2E gate to one env var) → [#1144](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1144); **#1136** `purge_otp_codes` beat crontab (daily 03:37 UTC, staggered; review caught that an unguarded `<=0` retention would instantly delete LIVE codes — service-side no-op guard + test added, sibling-sweep pattern) → [#1145](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1145) |
| ⬜ | Queued next: [#1139](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1139) first-login profile completion (display name — OTP JIT-provisioning leaves it NULL forever) · [#1150](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1150) eval-stack OTP-by-default + bundled local inbox · docs close-out is this PR | — |

The case that actually happens is the FIRST `/me` being throttled, where there is no cached answer to hold and the fix is to stay loading and retry — a different shape from the issue's sketch. **Writing the test is what exposed it**, which is the session's recurring lesson arriving from the other direction: not a test that proves nothing, but a test that refuses to be written because the behaviour isn't there.) (all six slice checkboxes ticked). 11 PRs merged across 2026-08-01/02:
#1129 (#1127 per-IP auth class) · #1131 (#735 step 1) · #1134 (#734 core) ·

#1151 (#1128 `/mcp` pat_only mode) · #1152 (docs close). Ledger:
docs/progress.md §Backlog track — ADR 0032.

## Open follow-ups (as of close)
- **#1139** first-login profile completion (OTP JIT provisioning leaves
  `users.display_name` NULL forever; PATCH /me + skippable prompt) — in flight.
- **#1141** verify-side timing channel (narrower sibling of #1137).
- **#1146** mailer CA-bundle/TLS-mode option (private-CA relays unusable).
- **#1147** pre-flight endpoint lacks mailer-appropriate throttle (generic 300/min
  token class vs 10/min auth class).
- **#1150** eval-stack OTP-by-default + bundled local inbox (MailHog-style) —
  user-prompted design 2026-08-02; decision recorded in the issue: no production
  mailbox bundling ever (deliverability/abuse), local inbox yes, bypass stays the
  DEV-loop default. Awaiting user go-ahead.

## Design facts worth remembering
- **No sign-up form, by design**: allowlist-gated (`AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS/_DOMAINS`,
  decision 5 — no open registration), first `otp/verify` JIT-provisions the user with
  email only (`resolve_or_create_user`, one-row-per-normalized-email linking).
- **/mcp mode ladder** (`mcp_auth_mode()`: azure_ad → pat_only → dev_bypass →
  disabled) mirrors `core.auth` exactly; in pat_only the JWT verifier is genuinely
  `None` (non-PAT bearer reaches no validator); OTP outranks dev-bypass in BOTH.
- **Floor**: `AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_MIN_SECONDS=1.0`, monotonic remainder-sleep, errors
  deliberately unpadded, 0 disables (re-opens #1137).

## Gotchas proven this track (beyond the ones in the old note)
- **smtplib `__exit__` sends QUIT and can RAISE** (`SMTPResponseException` on
  non-221) — a `with smtp` body's exception gets REPLACED; guard the whole
  statement or use explicit `quit()`-in-`finally`. Test fakes with never-raising
  `__exit__` structurally cannot see this (driver-boundary shape again).
- **Auth mode binds at IMPORT time** (`core/auth.py`); mode-matrix tests need
  env-before-import + explicit `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS`/`AZURE_*` teardown — one #1151
  test passed only because the suite-wide bypass rescued it (revert-testing caught it).
- **conftest env redirects must precede the `backend.app.*` imports** —
  `db.session` builds its engine at import; setting DATABASE_URL after is a no-op.
- **CodeQL FP classes seen**: warn-once module flag ("unused global"), late-binding
  `clock=lambda: _now()` ("unnecessary lambda" — the lambda is load-bearing for
  monkeypatched clocks), test-double `__init__` skipping super ("missing init").

1. **Backend** — `PATCH /api/v1/me` (`backend/app/api/v1/me.py`, `backend/app/services/user_service.py`): validates `display_name` non-empty-after-strip and ≤256 chars (matches the `String(256)` column), behind the same `get_current_user` dependency the GET handler uses — no mode branching, so it works identically for a cookie session, a PAT, or an AAD token.
2. **Frontend** — a skippable, one-time completion prompt (`ProfileCompletionPrompt.tsx`) plus an inline edit affordance on the Profile page for every mode, sharing one hook (`useSaveDisplayName.ts`) and a new `MeUpdateContext` so a save updates state without a second `GET /me`.

## Design decisions

- **One-time/skip semantics**: gated on `sessionStorage` (`dataq:profileCompletionPrompt:skipped`), not React state — survives a reload of the tab but clears when it closes, which is what "session" means to a user. Closing any other way (Esc/X) counts as skip too; there's no separate "undecided" state.
- **otp mode identity refresh**: in `otp` mode the header name comes from `OtpSessionProvider`'s own captured `/me`, not `MeContext` — so `useSaveDisplayName` also calls the existing `adopt()` (already used by verify) to keep the header in sync. - **Editable in every mode** (Profile page, via antd `Typography.Text editable`): an AAD user's *header* still shows the token's name (untouched), but the stored row — what shares/admin lists render — is now overridable there too.

Implementing the AAD-override half of the issue surfaced a real bug: `_upsert_user`/`_claim_unlinked_user` in `backend/app/core/auth.py` ran on **every** real-mode request (no session cache) and unconditionally overwrote `display_name` from the AAD token's `name` claim — silently reverting a `PATCH /me` override on the user's very next request. Fixed both to `COALESCE` onto the existing value (seed on first login, never re-sync over a set value) rather than defer/file, since it directly broke this issue's stated AC. Updated the one pre-existing test (`test_identity_conflict.py`) that encoded the old overwrite behavior, and added regression coverage in `test_auth.py`.

**Commit `2280299e`** (backend) — Replaced the COALESCE display-name guard with an explicit override flag:
- **Migration `6230293aea96`** — `backend/alembic/versions/6230293aea96_add_users_display_name_override.py`: additive `users.display_name_override BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false`. Verified up → down → up against scratch DB `dataq_test_1139`, and confirmed the parity test (`test_migration_parity.py`) passes.
- `_upsert_user`/`_claim_unlinked_user` (`backend/app/core/auth.py`) now branch on the flag via SQL `CASE` instead of `COALESCE`: sync the AAD claim into `display_name` whenever `display_name_override` is `False`, leave it alone whenever `True`. The `IntegrityError→409 identity_conflict` path is byte-identical (verified by diff — only the `display_name` value expression changed).
- `user_service.update_display_name` (called from `PATCH /me`) now sets `display_name_override = True`.
- **Override-clear semantics chosen**: `PATCH /me` never resets the flag to `False` because `MeUpdate` rejects empty/whitespace-only input — there is no "clear the name" operation today, so nothing to reset it for. Documented inline in `user_service.py` for whoever adds a clear path later (should reset the flag alongside).
- Both directions pinned in `test_auth.py` (`test_upsert_preserves_a_patch_me_override_across_relogin`, `test_upsert_syncs_an_aad_rename_when_there_is_no_override`) and `test_identity_conflict.py` (`test_an_aad_signin_does_not_overwrite_a_pre_set_otp_display_name`, `test_a_second_aad_signin_after_adoption_respects_an_override`, plus the existing tests updated to assert `display_name_override` explicitly) — including the `_claim_unlinked_user` coverage the review flagged as missing.

**Commit `40dfc173`** (frontend) — Fixed `Profile.tsx`'s unchanged-value guard to compare the edited text against `name` (the rendered value — `display_name ?? email`) instead of the nullable `display_name`, which previously let a bare blur PATCH a null-display_name user's own email in as their display name. **Design decisions:**
- `AUTH_EMAIL_TLS_MODE` (`starttls` default/unchanged, `implicit` for SMTPS `:465` via `smtplib.SMTP_SSL`, `none` plaintext test-only) and `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE` (PEM path, boot-time-validated to exist) added to `backend/app/core/config.py`, wired through the shared `_deliver` ladder in `backend/app/services/otp_mailer.py` used by both `send_code` and `send_preflight`.
- **No insecure-verify option was added** — recorded in the PR body per instruction: a private CA bundle covers the legitimate case; weakening verification was rejected as a shortcut.
- `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE` is scoped per-send (`ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...)` builds a fresh context each call) — never the process-wide trust store, unlike the `SSL_CERT_FILE` footgun it replaces.
- Implicit-mode TLS/cert failures classify as the `connect` stage, not `tls`, documented in code because `smtplib.SMTP_SSL`'s constructor does connect+handshake together with no separate hook — pinned with a dedicated test.
- Simplified the e2e-otp lane (`scripts/e2e-otp-stack.sh`, CI) from `SSL_CERT_FILE` to `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE`, live-verified (not just reasoned) against the real sink — genuine STARTTLS handshake, real cert verification, code retrieved via the sink's capture API.

<result>## Summary

Implemented issue #1146 as **PR #1155**: https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1155 (milestone `v1.1 Backlog`, not auto-merged).

**Design decisions:**
- `AUTH_EMAIL_TLS_MODE` (`starttls` default/unchanged, `implicit` for SMTPS `:465` via `smtplib.SMTP_SSL`, `none` plaintext test-only) and `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE` (PEM path, boot-time-validated to exist) added to `backend/app/core/config.py`, wired through the shared `_deliver` ladder in `backend/app/services/otp_mailer.py` used by both `send_code` and `send_preflight`.
- **No insecure-verify option was added** — recorded in the PR body per instruction: a private CA bundle covers the legitimate case; weakening verification was rejected as a shortcut.
- `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE` is scoped per-send (`ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...)` builds a fresh context each call) — never the process-wide trust store, unlike the `SSL_CERT_FILE` footgun it replaces.
- Implicit-mode TLS/cert failures classify as the `connect` stage, not `tls`, documented in code because `smtplib.SMTP_SSL`'s constructor does connect+handshake together with no separate hook — pinned with a dedicated test.
- Simplified the e2e-otp lane (`scripts/e2e-otp-stack.sh`, CI) from `SSL_CERT_FILE` to `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE`, live-verified (not just reasoned) against the real sink — genuine STARTTLS handshake, real cert verification, code retrieved via the sink's capture API.

**Test evidence:** black/ruff/mypy/bandit all clean; full backend suite `3533 passed, 1 skipped`, 97.06% coverage (gate 80%); 61 tests in the two touched test files including implicit-mode/CA-bundle/none-mode/boot-failure cases, with the CA-bundle test monkeypatching `smtplib.SMTP` (the transport) rather than `ssl.create_default_context` (the seam under test), verified via a real self-signed cert and `SSLContext.get_ca_certs()`.

**Docs updated:** `deploy/README.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, `.env.app.example`, plus `backend/scripts/e2e_otp_smtp_sink.py` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments.

**Found and fixed in the same PR:** the mandated `/code-review` pass (3 parallel independent agents — CLAUDE.md compliance, bug scan, git-history/prior-PR-comment check) caught one real issue — `frontend/e2e-otp/README.md` was left stale, still describing `SSL_CERT_FILE` and #1146 as unresolved. Fixed via a follow-up commit (`e177d282`) and posted to the PR. One self-caught slip along the way: my first review comment cited a fabricated commit SHA for the fix link — caught and corrected via `gh api ... -X PATCH` before reporting done.

No other issues found or deferred.</result>

<result>Sanity check: re-verified all three findings against the new head SHA (`admin_service.py` was byte-identical across the fixup; the key-separation test unchanged), and confirmed via the API that all three inline comments landed on the intended lines (362, 368, 618).

Posted review: https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1156#pullrequestreview-4839963197

**Findings posted (3, after filtering 6 candidates at the ≥80 confidence bar):**

1. **Shared circuit-breaker state** (`admin_service.py:362`) — `enforce_preflight_quota` calls `otp_service.get_counter_store()`, the module-level *singleton*, so the pre-flight throttle shares one `CircuitBreaker` and Redis client with the sign-in mail-bomb quota. Enough Redis errors from admin pre-flight traffic trips the shared breaker and silently fails open the public unauthenticated `/auth/otp/request` cap for the open window. This is the exact coupling #1140 (issue #1135) built `core/circuit_breaker.py` to prevent one day earlier; `RedisOtpCounterStore`'s docstring states breaker state is per-instance "deliberately so", and `core/rate_limit.py` honours it with a private `_BREAKER`. The code's own comment calling this "two independent budgets" is true for counters but false for availability. Found independently by three of the five review agents.

2. **Unconditional fail-open logging** (`admin_service.py:368`) — no warn-once suppression, unlike both sibling implementations (`otp_service._counter_unavailable_warned`, `rate_limit._warn_store_unavailable_once`, commented "avoid a log flood on outage"). When the store is down the throttle is failing *open*, so it caps nothing; a hot loop plus degraded Redis is a warning per request — the shape that caused the 2026-07-13 Celery-starvation outage.

3. **Vacuous key-separation test** (`test_admin.py:618`) — the test never invokes `/auth/otp/request`, so `assert not any(k.startswith("otp:req:"))` cannot fail for the reason its name claims. It proves the pre-flight key prefix, not budget separation.

**Summary of this round's investigation and fix:**

**Failing test:** `tests/auth/OtpSessionProvider.test.tsx > OtpSessionProvider — other auth modes > is a passthrough in dev_bypass mode and never probes /me` (job 91559474682, run 30771559194).

**Determination:** Real order-dependence, not the #573/#1123 antd/userEvent slow-runner flake — evidence: (1) it's a test I already touched, not an untouched one; (2) the failure was a clean `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` — my previous `probeSession.mockResolvedValue(null)` default fix had converted what was previously a crash into exactly this clean assertion failure, proving `probeSession()` really was being invoked; (3) it reproduced on 2 of 2 real CI runs and never once locally across 20+ full-suite runs at varying concurrency (default, `--maxWorkers=1`, `--no-file-parallelism`).

**Root cause:** `OtpSessionProvider — other auth modes` called `vi.doMock('../../src/auth/config', () => ({ authMode: mode }))` inside the test body, but the file's top-level `beforeEach` *also* `vi.doMock`s the exact same module path with `'otp'` (for every other describe block). Both registrations are real and racing each other for the same module id; under CI's timing the re-registration occasionally lost, so `ActiveOtpSessionProvider` mounted instead of the passthrough and called `probeSession()` while the mock was still reporting `authMode: 'otp'`.

**Fix:** Stopped mocking `config` a second time entirely. The test now drives the *real* `config.ts` via `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__` (ADR 0028's runtime-config contract) — the same proven pattern `CurrentUserProvider.test.tsx` already uses — with `vi.doUnmock('../../src/auth/config')` clearing the outer `beforeEach`'s registration first. There is now exactly one source of truth for `authMode` in this test, so the race is structurally eliminated rather than papered over.

**Verified locally:** `pnpm typecheck`/`pnpm lint` clean; the file alone and the full suite (88/88 files, 869/869 tests) green across 3 runs, including under `--maxWorkers=1` and `--no-file-parallelism`.

## Round 5 — final report

**Root cause (confirmed via downloaded artifacts, not guessed):** Downloaded `playwright-report` from run 30772437357 (`gh run download 30772437357 -n playwright-report`) and read `error-context.md` for both failing specs (`session.spec.ts:21` and `:51`). Both page snapshots showed the app **fully signed in on `/dashboard`** with the **"Welcome to DataQ" modal still open** and "Skip for now" active — execution never got past the dismiss step inside `signIn.complete()`. Critically, unlike every earlier `click()`-timeout in this PR, the error carried **no locator call log** — just `Test timeout of 90000ms exceeded.` — the signature of a hung plain `Promise`, not a retrying locator action. That pointed straight at `page.waitForResponse()`: despite its own explicit `{ timeout: 20_000 }` + `.catch(() => null)`, it never resolved within the full 90s budget, on two separate CI runs (30772079151, 30772437357), while passing every single time locally. This is the coordinator's hypothesis (3).

**Fix:** Removed `page.waitForResponse()` and the `/me` network sync point entirely. Replaced it with pure UI polling: `locator.waitFor({ state: 'visible' })` achieves the same synchronization without depending on Playwright's response-event timing, and now **every** wait in the dismiss block carries its own explicit timeout (25s visible, 5s click, 5s hidden) so nothing can silently inherit and exhaust the whole project timeout.

{"body":"## Summary

- **`otp` is now what you boot into; `bypass` is the explicit downgrade.** Both compose stacks (`docker-compose.yml` and the published `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`) default to email one-time codes (ADR [0032](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/adr/0032-email-otp-signin.md)) instead of dev-bypass. An eval stack's defaults **are** the security posture people actually run — the same argument that flipped the default secret store off the plaintext one (ADR 0039) — and `bypass` by default meant anyone who could reach the port administered a tool that stores warehouse credentials.
- **A bundled local inbox is what makes that default viable.** [Mailpit](https://mailpit.axllent.org) (MIT, pinned `v1.30.6`) catches every message at `localhost:8025`, so the SMTP relay `otp` used to require is gone: DataQ runs its **real** mailer over a **real** SMTP `connect → AUTH → send`, and the code lands in a web inbox on your machine. Nothing leaves the host, no mailbox has to exist.
- **One switch, `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL`** — `scripts/setup.sh` asks for it and writes it to the gitignored `.env`. An address turns OTP on and makes you the workspace admin; **set-but-empty** is the explicit dev-bypass downgrade; **unset** stops compose and names both options, because a permissive auth posture should be a decision somebody made rather than the one they got by not reading.

## Linked issue

Fixes #1150

## Type of change

- [x] feat — new functionality
- [ ] fix — bug fix (linked issue above)
- [ ] chore — repo housekeeping / tooling
- [ ] docs — documentation only
- [ ] refactor — no behaviour change
- [ ] test — test-only change

**Mailpit, not MailHog** (both MIT, both rule-40 clear; #1149 named MailHog/smtp4dev). `OtpMailer` **always** performs an SMTP `AUTH` exchange, and MailHog advertises `AUTH` only when handed a bcrypt credential file — which would mean shipping a credential in a tracked file (CLAUDE.md §11). Mailpit's `MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY` needs no file. MailHog is also unreleased since 2020; Mailpit shipped `v1.30.6` on 2026-07-28. Licence verified from the repository's own metadata (`axllent/mailpit` → SPDX `MIT`), not from a README claim.

**Why all six `AUTH_EMAIL_*` values are `${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL:+…}` rather than one flag per key.** The backend refuses to boot on a *partially* configured mailer block (ADR 0032 decision 2), so a per-variable switch would turn the documented downgrade into a crash lo","failing":["GitGuardian Security Checks"],"head":"b9c97bd2","mergeState":"UNSTABLE","milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","pending":[]}

## Review summary — PR #1159 (b9c97bd2)

**Verdict: none.** No defects found across either audit.

### (a) CLAUDE.md compliance — clean
- **No credentials in tracked files**: verified `.env.example`, `.env.app.example`, both compose files, `setup.sh`, and `seed_local_smtp_secret.py` — every secret-shaped value (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `OPENBAO_TOKEN`, the SMTP password) ships blank/unpopulated in tracked files; `setup.sh` generates real values only into the gitignored `.env`/`.env.app`; the SMTP password is generated in-process by `seed_local_smtp_secret.py` and never printed or written to a tracked file (it even avoids logging the *secret name* to dodge a CodeQL taint false-positive).
- **ADR 0032 fail-closed contract intact**: `backend/app/core/config.py` `_validate_otp_auth` (model_validator) checks all 4 required `AUTH_EMAIL_*` fields plus the allowlist and raises at boot on any partial state. The compose templating (`${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL:+…}`) conditions all 6 `AUTH_EMAIL_*` vars on the *same* switch, so it structurally cannot produce a partial block. I verified this mechanically with `docker compose config` (not just by reading): unset → refuses to start with the documented message; set-but-empty → all 6 vars blank simultaneously; set to an address → all 6 populated + `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` correctly includes it. Confirmed identical behavior in both `docker-compose.yml` and `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`.
- **CI/dev-loop lanes untouched**: PR's changed-file list has zero `.github/workflows/` or `frontend/e2e*` entries — confirmed via `gh pr diff --name-only`.

### (b) Shallow bug scan — no big bugs
- **Three-state switch**: mechanically verified correct (above), including the `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` trailing-comma artifact in bypass mode (`dev-bypass@dataq.local,`) — harmless, since `workspace_admin_email_set` filters empty parts after `.split(",")`.
- **Seeder absent-only semantics** (`backend/scripts/seed_local_smtp_secret.py`): cannot clobber a real secret — it only writes on `SecretNotFoundError`, and explicitly refuses to write (exits 1) on `SecretStoreUnavailableError` per the ADR 0039 "an outage must never look like unset" rule. TOCTOU window between `get`/`set` exists in theory but is a non-issue given the one-shot, single-container `restart: "no"` design.
- **setup.sh regressions**: `set_env_kv` correctly distinguishes "key absent" (append) vs "key present-blank" (rewrite) vs "already set" (leave alone), so re-running against a pre-#1150 `.env` lacking `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` correctly triggers the prompt once and is idempotent thereafter.
- **`seed_dev.py` OTP-operator share**: grants `edit` only (never `admin`/`owner`, enforced by `share_service`), and the shared operator is already a `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` member via the same compose switch — so the share doesn't expand privilege, it just avoids landing the evaluator in an empty non-admin suite list. Scoped to dev/eval paths only (`setup.sh` and `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`'s migrate step); confirmed it's absent from the CI/prod deploy paths (grepped `deploy/` and workflows).
- **`AUTH_EMAIL_TLS_MODE=none` for Mailpit**: correct, not a STARTTLS mismatch — `otp_mailer.py`'s `_deliver` skips `server.starttls()` entirely for `tls_mode == "none"` and logs a loud warning on every send; Mailpit's `MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY` + `MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE` only advertise AUTH over a plaintext connection, so `starttls` mode would have failed against it.
- **Frontend `config.ts` precedence change**: this PR *fixes* a real pre-existing bug rather than introducing one — the old order (`bypass ? … : otp ? …`) meant `VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true` (the long-standing compose default) always won over `VITE_AUTH_MODE=otp`, so OTP mode was unreachable in the dev stack before this reorder.
- Noted but not reported (documented, not a defect): `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` requires *two* separate variables (`DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=` and `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass`) for the full downgrade, since the frontend's injected enum has no boolean companion there. Clearing only `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` leaves the backend in dev-bypass while the frontend still shows an OTP screen (whose endpoints 503) — but this is explicitly called out in both `config.ts`'s doc comment and `docs/getting-started.md`, and doesn't change the actual security boundary (same loopback-only, same "everyone is admin" posture as the correctly-downgraded state).

### Finding 1 (confirmed, high confidence): "clear `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` to point the compose stack at a REAL relay" does not work — the documented escape hatch silently blanks the mailer instead

- `docker-compose.yml` (post-PR) lines 37–41 (comment) and line 45 (`AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST: ${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL:+mailpit}` inside the `x-otp-auth-env` anchor, merged into `api`/`worker`/`otp-mail-secret` via `<<: *otp-auth-env`)
- `.env.app.example` lines 88–95 (identical claim)

**Claim in the comments:**
> "These `environment:` values SHADOW anything you put in `.env.app`... Clear DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL and the override goes away, leaving whatever you set here — that is how you point the compose stack at a REAL relay... with the switch empty, nothing here overrides it."

**Evidence it's false:** Every `AUTH_EMAIL_*` key in `x-otp-auth-env` is written as `${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL:+value}`. This form always emits the key into the `environment:` map — as `""` when `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` is empty, never absent. I verified this empirically with the actual PR files:

```
$ cat .env        # DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=  (cleared, per the documented instructions)
$ cat .env.app     # AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST=smtp.myrealrelay.example.com  (a "real relay")
$ docker compose config

  worker:         AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST: ""     ← blanked
  otp-mail-secret: AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST: ""    ← blanked
  migrate:        AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST: smtp.myrealrelay.example.com   ← only this one is correct, and it's the one service that doesn't need it
```

`migrate` only "works" by accident, because it's the one service that was *not* given `<<: *otp-auth-env`. The three services that actually consume the mailer config (`api`, which sends OTP codes; `worker`, which shares the block; `otp-mail-secret`, which provisions the SMTP password) all get their real-relay settings silently discarded and fall back through `_validate_otp_auth`'s "untouched" path to plain `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS`. Not a pre-existing issue — it's new in this PR (the `x-otp-auth-env` anchor and its accompanying claim are introduced here) and not tracked by any existing issue (checked #1146/#1147/#1149/#1150).

**Fix direction:** either drop the "point at a real relay via `.env.app`" claim (the compose stack fundamentally can't support that with unconditional `${VAR:+...}` entries merged over `env_file`), or restructure so the mailer block is only merged into `environment:` when `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` is actually set (e.g. a second override file, or moving the mailer vars out of the merged anchor and into a conditional `env_file` layering), or explicitly instruct the operator to edit `docker-compose.yml`'s `x-otp-auth-env` block itself rather than `.env.app`.

Mailpit's `MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY` needs no file. MailHog is also unreleased since 2020.

**Bypass opt-in: one switch, `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL`.** An address → OTP; **set-but-empty** → explicit dev-bypass downgrade; **unset** → compose refuses and names both (`${VAR?msg}`, not `:?`, is what distinguishes decision from omission). `setup.sh` prompts and writes it to the gitignored `.env`.

**Two seams the design forced:** (1) the mailer has no "no password" path, so a one-shot `otp-mail-secret` service generates one into the in-memory vault on every `up`, **never overwriting an existing value**; (2) blank `AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_PORT`/`TLS_MODE` now fall back to defaults instead of an int/`Literal` parse crash — the only two non-`str|None` keys in the block; fail-closed contract untouched (neither is in `_AUTH_EMAIL_REQUIRED`), pinned by test.

### Live-validated vs config-validated

**Live** (real stack, isolated project + remapped ports; the developer's own stack untouched): `otp/request` → code in the catcher inbox → `otp/verify` → session cookie → `/me` `is_workspace_admin: true` → `GET /suites` returns all 5 seeded suites. Downgrade path re-booted clean as `auth_dev_bypass_active`. **Security property verified rather than assumed:** with `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true` still set alongside a complete OTP block, `/me` with no credential answers **401** — dev-bypass does not leak through.

**Config-validated:** `docker compose config` on both files across four states (OTP / empty / unset / real-relay override).

### Three findings I fixed in-PR

1. **Empty-workspace regression** (my own review pass; only a live sign-in could show it) — all seeded rows are owned by the dev-bypass identity, so signing in as yourself landed in an empty app against a README promising demo data. `seed_dev` now `edit`-shares each seeded suite with the allow-listed address (`edit` because admin/owner are ungrantable by design). 10 tests incl. "a suite owned by somebody else is never touched".
2. **CodeQL 4× high** `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` — the seeder printed the secret's *name*. Removed the flow rather than annotating it away.

gh issue create --repo TheurgicDuke771/DataQ --title "test(e2e-otp): session revocation specs flaky in CI — session.spec.ts:51/:71 time out intermittently on main" --label bug --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --body "Observed 2026-08-03 on run 30773569973 — a **docs-only** PR (#1157), so the flake is main's, not any PR's. The two revoked-session specs (\`e2e-otp/session.spec.ts:51\` 'drops the app WITHOUT a navigation on the next API 401' and \`:71\` 'signing out revokes the session and the back button cannot undo it') failed after all retries with click/timeout exhaustion, while the other 9 OTP-lane specs pass consistently.

History (PR #1153's CI saga, 5 rounds): fixed in sequence — profile-prompt modal intercepting clicks (fixtures dismissal), a flat 5s wait racing MeProvider's /me fetch (waitForResponse sync), an order-dependent double vi.doMock (vitest side), a waitForResponse that can never resolve when armed late (replaced with UI polling), and a 90s otp-project budget. #1153's own final run was green; main now shows the residual: the two specs that revoke a session server-side mid-test still intermittently exhaust their budget.

Suspects not yet ruled out: the revocation helper's API call racing the app's own 401 handling; the profile-prompt dismissal state (sessionStorage) interacting with the second sign-in these specs perform; Mailpit-vs-sink timing after #1155 moved the lane to AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE. The fix should make the specs deterministic (sync on observable state, not sleeps), not raise budgets further.

Blocks: any PR's required Playwright check, intermittently (currently #1157/#1159 both hit it).

## Summary — Issue #1160, PR #1161

**Root cause:** Confirmed via the CI artifact (downloaded `playwright-report` from run 30773569973, read `error-context.md` for both `session.spec.ts:51` and `:71`). Both page snapshots showed the "Welcome to DataQ" profile-completion prompt sitting **open and pristine** (empty input, untouched Skip button) for the entire 90s test budget — with `157 × ... retrying click action ... waiting 500ms` on the downstream click, confirming the modal blocked it for essentially the whole run, every time (near-100% reproduction across 4 CI runs on two different PRs, per the coordinator's update).

`signIn.complete()`'s dismiss step (from PR #1153) waited only 25s for the prompt to become visible before swallowing a timeout and returning "successfully." On CI's slower/shared hardware, `MeProvider`'s separate `/me` fetch (which the prompt's visibility depends on) apparently sometimes takes longer than that — so the wait gave up *before* the prompt rendered, then the prompt appeared moments later and sat there blocking whatever the spec clicked next, a full minute downstream from the real cause. This never reproduced locally (even matching CI's exact `--workers=1` concurrency) because `/me` resolves in under a second on this hardware every time — consistent with a hardware-latency gap, not a logic bug.

**Fix:**
1. Removed the fixed sub-budget and the swallowing try/catch entirely. With no `timeout` option and no `use.actionTimeout` configured, a Playwright locator action is bounded only by the test's own 90s project timeout, so the wait now polls for as long as the test legitimately can — and a genuine failure now points straight at "the prompt never rendered" instead of a misleading downstream click failure. No sleeps, no budget raises — this removes an arbitrary early give-up rather than adding a bigger number.
2. Added a shared `revokeServerSide()` helper in `session.spec.ts` that polls the old session token against `GET /me` until it observably 401s before either revocation spec drives the UI — defense-in-depth per the issue's suspect list, confirming the revocation is observable rather than merely inferred from the 204 (code inspection shows `session_service.revoke()` already commits synchronously before the response, so this wasn't the root cause, but it removes all residual doubt).

**Verified locally:** real backend stack (own Postgres DB, migrations applied, SMTP sink + otp-mode api), matching CI's exact concurrency (`CI=1 --workers=1`) — **11/11 green across two consecutive runs**. input.message: Round 2 on #1161 (run 30786514095): the failure MOVED and got worse — now ALL THREE session specs (:21 which always passed, :50, :70) fail with `locator.waitFor: Test timeout of 90000ms exceeded`. Diagnosis from the shape: your unbounded `waitFor(visible)` on the prompt hangs forever whenever the prompt legitimately NEVER appears — and it's conditional by design (otp mode + display_name still NULL + no sessionStorage skip). If these specs' sign-in reuses an identity whose display_name is already set (check: do the session specs share an email with an earlier spec — or with the seeded operator whose name seed_dev or a prior prompt-save populated? also check whether any spec SAVES the prompt rather than skipping), the modal never renders and an unconditional wait is a guaranteed 90s hang — which also explains why the artifact earlier showed it 'open and pristine' in some runs (name-null identity) and now never-appearing (name-set identity): the prompt's appearance depends on per-email DB state that varies with spec order/parallelism. ALSO make identity deterministic: if specs share emails across the file/lane, give each spec a unique address (the allowlist is domain-based or per-spec-configurable — check the lane's env) so per-email DB state can't couple specs; that kills the whole class. Download this run's artifacts to confirm which state the page was in at timeout before you commit to the diagnosis. Verify locally by running the lane TWICE back-to-back against the SAME database (state persistence across runs is exactly the coupling), plus once with workers>1 if the config allows. Plain push to the #1161 branch. Report what the artifact showed + the fix.

content.text: why the playwright failing so many times? are you not testing it locally before CI?

Fair question, and it deserves a straight answer: **yes, every single push was tested locally first** — the full lane ran 11/11 green, usually twice back-to-back, and later rounds even matched CI's exact `--workers=1` concurrency before pushing. The gate wasn't skipped. The problem is that this failure class is one the local environment *structurally cannot reproduce*, and it took too many rounds to admit that:

**Why local green kept lying:**
- The core trigger is hardware latency. Locally, the `/me` fetch behind the profile-completion modal resolves in under a second, every time. On GitHub's shared runners it can take 25+ seconds. The race window that breaks CI **does not exist** on the dev machine — no number of local reruns could open it.
- The just-confirmed deeper cause is worse: the modal's appearance depends on **per-email database state** (it only renders while `display_name` is NULL), so spec ordering and identity reuse decide whether it shows up late or never. A fresh local database in a fixed order produces one world; CI's accumulated state produces the other. Each fix was correct for the world its evidence came from and wrong in the other.

**Why so many rounds:** they weren't one bug re-failing — CI peeled off six real, distinct defects in sequence (modal intercepting clicks → flat 5s wait racing `/me` → a vitest double-`doMock` race → a `waitForResponse` that can hang permanently → the budget red herring → an unconditional wait that hangs when the modal never appears). Each fix unmasked the next. That's typical of E2E stabilization, but not blameless.

**My honest self-criticism as orchestrator:** this is exactly the project's own recorded lesson — the #953 rule ("for anything that crosses an environment boundary, only a live run is evidence") and the W4 retro ("a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing"). Local runs here *encode fast hardware* the same way the old fixtures encoded our model. After round 2, I should have stopped accepting "green locally twice" as sufficient and demanded either CI-condition reproduction (CPU-throttled runs, injected `/me` latency) or a state-independent design — which is what the current fix finally is: race "modal or app-chrome, whichever renders first" and unique per-spec identities, correct in *both* worlds instead of tuned for one.

If this round doesn't hold, the right next step is not an eighth timing fix — it's making the prompt's precondition explicit in the fixture (seed or assert the `display_name` state per spec) so the test controls the state instead of discovering it.

content.text:
Update — and a correction to my last diagnosis: the artifacts **contradicted** the identity-reuse hypothesis. The specs already use unique per-spec emails, the prompt *does* appear, and the click *does* fire — but "Skip for now" then **stays visible for the full 90 seconds** (177 consecutive visible-resolutions after the click). Best-supported explanation: the one-shot click lands on a DOM node React has just swapped out (a detached-node click fires no handler), which a retry heals and a single click never can. The fix is a `toPass()` retry loop — re-click against the current DOM every ~500ms, no sleeps, no budget change — verified locally including two back-to-back runs against the same database and a multi-worker run. CI is running on the new commit.

If *this* fails the same way — button visibly clicked repeatedly and never closing — the suspect stops being the test and becomes the app's Skip handler itself under CI conditions, and that's where we'd look next (exactly the "make the test control the state, or fix the app" fork I mentioned).

- The OTP Playwright lane fails on SHARED-RUNNER latency and PER-EMAIL DB STATE
  (profile prompt renders only while display_name IS NULL) — local green proves
  nothing for either axis; the #953 rule applies to CI hardware too.
- A conditional UI element must be handled with a RACE (`modal.or(chrome).waitFor()`
  + branch), never an unconditional wait (hangs when it legitimately never shows)
  and never a swallowed try/catch (converts a blocked page into a downstream
  mystery). One-shot clicks on React-rerendering DOM need `expect(...).toPass()`
  retry loops — a detached-node click fires no handler.
- `${VAR:+…}` compose templating ALWAYS emits the key ("" when unset) and
  `environment:` beats `env_file:` — an "unset it to override via env_file" claim
  is structurally false; nest defaults `${SWITCH:+${VAR:-default}}` instead
  (verified against the real CLI; the #1159 review caught this producing a
  silently-unauthenticated stack).

(all six slice checkboxes ticked). 11 PRs merged across 2026-08-01/02:
#1129 (#1127 per-IP auth class) · #1131 (#735 step 1) · #1134 (#734 core) ·

## Open follow-ups (state at 2026-08-02 session end; user asked ALL of these closed)
- **#1139 / PR #1153** — profile completion built (PATCH /me + `display_name_override`
  flag migration `6230293aea96` after review found COALESCE froze AAD renames; also
  fixed AAD claim-sync clobbering overrides + a Profile.tsx blur-PATCHes-email guard
  bug). PR open, auto-merge ARMED, blocked on ONE CI failure:
  `OtpSessionProvider.test.tsx` dev-bypass passthrough test, `undefined.then` —
  suspected order-dependent mock leakage (868/869 pass). Fix agent relaunched.
- **#1141** verify-side timing floor + **#1147** pre-flight throttle — one Opus agent,
  2 PRs, relaunched (nothing pushed before session limit).
- **#1146** mailer TLS-mode/CA-bundle — Sonnet agent relaunched (nothing pushed).
- **#1150** eval-stack OTP-by-default + bundled inbox — **HELD**: its Agent launch was
  the tool call the user REJECTED at session end; do not relaunch without explicit
  go-ahead. #1149 (duplicate scope, filed same day) closed as dup of #1150 with
  carry-over comment. Decision recorded in issue: never bundle a production mailbox
  (deliverability/abuse); local mail catcher yes; CI/dev-loop bypass lanes unchanged.
- Review flow discipline held all session: /code-review panels per PR; #1153's review
  found 3 real defects (COALESCE freeze, blur-guard, untested _claim COALESCE) — all
  fixed in-PR. Pyright cross-worktree noise is expected while agents run — CI is the
  arbiter. Session-limit interruptions twice: on renewal, stopped-by-user agents
  CANNOT be resumed via SendMessage — relaunch fresh agents instead.

## Design facts worth remembering
- **No sign-up form, by design**: allowlist-gated (`AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS/_DOMAINS`,
  decision 5 — no open registration), first `otp/verify` JIT-provisions the user with
  email only (`resolve_or_create_user`, one-row-per-normalized-email linking).
- **/mcp mode ladder** (`mcp_auth_mode()`: azure_ad → pat_only → dev_bypass →
  disabled) mirrors `core.auth` exactly; in pat_only the JWT verifier is genuinely
  `None` (non-PAT bearer reaches no validator); OTP outranks dev-bypass in BOTH.
- **Floor**: `AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_MIN_SECONDS=1.0`, monotonic remainder-sleep, errors
  deliberately unpadded, 0 disables (re-opens #1137).

## Gotchas proven this track (beyond the ones in the old note)
- **smtplib `__exit__` sends QUIT and can RAISE** (`SMTPResponseException` on
  non-221) — a `with smtp` body's exception gets REPLACED; guard the whole
  statement or use explicit `quit()`-in-`finally`. Test fakes with never-raising
  `__exit__` structurally cannot see this (driver-boundary shape again).
- **Auth mode binds at IMPORT time** (`core/auth.py`); mode-matrix tests need
  env-before-import + explicit `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS`/`AZURE_*` teardown — one #1151
  test passed only because the suite-wide bypass rescued it (revert-testing caught it).
- **conftest env redirects must precede the `backend.app.*` imports** —
  `db.session` builds its engine at import; setting DATABASE_URL after is a no-op.
- **CodeQL FP classes seen**: warn-once module flag ("unused global"), late-binding
  `clock=lambda: _now()` ("unnecessary lambda" — the lambda is load-bearing for
  monkeypatched clocks), test-double `__init__` skipping super ("missing init").
  Dismiss with reasons + resolve threads; unresolved bot threads BLOCK auto-merge
  ([[dev-review-thread-resolution-blocks-merge]]).
- **GitGuardian (non-required) stays red on a fake JWT in branch history** —
  verified against the 12 required checks before deciding; squash-merge keeps the
  literal off main; rationale recorded on PR #1151. betterleaks (required) passed —
  the [[dev-secret-in-branch-history]] rebuild rule is for REAL secrets it flags.
- Prod deploy note: OTP not yet flipped on in prod (runs `oidc`); the #1148 nginx
  XFP fix rides the frontend image — redeploy the frontend before enabling OTP
  anywhere TLS-terminated.
- Related: [[project_rate_limiting_725]], [[feedback_review_before_merge]],
  [[dev-stacked-pr-after-squash-merge]], [[feedback_verify_locally_before_push]].

1	# DataQ — deployment guide
2	
3	How DataQ v1 is deployed to Azure. Infrastructure is **in-repo OpenTofu**
4	(`deploy/terraform/azure/`, applied — [ADR 0024](../docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md));
5	the app rolls out via the **`Deploy`** workflow
6	([.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml), `workflow_dispatch`).
7	The stack is **live** — this is the runbook to provision a fresh environment and to
8	deploy a new image. Related: [ADR 0025](../docs/adr/0025-production-image-pip-slim.md)
9	(slim+pip image), [ADR 0023](../docs/adr/0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR).
10	
11	Azure is **one** deploy target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013) — the
12	manifests here are infra config, not business logic. No Azure resource names are
13	hardcoded in app code; they live only as OpenTofu vars + workflow `vars`/`secrets`.
14	
15	## Before you deploy: production prerequisites
16	
17	Read this before a production rollout. It's the "what must change, what access you
18	need, and what your cloud must provide" checklist; the [provisioning runbook](#one-time-provisioning)
19	below is the how.
20	
21	### 1. What you must change (never ship the eval/dev defaults)
22	
23	The prebuilt-image quickstart ([docs/getting-started](../docs/getting-started.md)) is a
24	**dev-bypass eval stack** — it disables auth, uses a passwordless DB, and binds to
25	loopback. A production deployment must flip all of the following. Values live in
26	[`deploy/.env.app.prod.example`](.env.app.prod.example) (app settings) +
27	[`deploy/terraform/azure/variables.tf`](terraform/azure/variables.tf) (infra):
28	
29	| Setting | Eval default | Production |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` | `true` | **`false`** — this is the master auth switch; leaving it on means **no authentication at all**. |
32	| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` / `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` / `AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID` | empty | your Azure AD tenant + the two app registrations (API + SPA). |
33	| **Frontend auth config** | `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` (eval) | the **same generic image**, reconfigured at **runtime** — `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` + `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` / `DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` (ADR 0028). **No rebuild** — nginx injects `/config.js` from env. See [frontend/Dockerfile](../frontend/Dockerfile). |
34	| `SECRET_STORE` | `openbao` (local/eval — ADR 0039) | **`azure_key_vault`** + `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL` + the managed identity's `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` (#408). |
35	| `DATABASE_URL` / `REDIS_URL` | inline, passwordless | Key Vault-backed Container Apps secrets — **never literals**; real credentials. |
36	| `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` | n/a (same-origin) | empty — the frontend Container App proxies `/api` same-origin (ADR 0028); set the SPA origin only if you split them. |
37	| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | n/a | the public origin — used to assemble inbound webhook URLs **and** the "View run" deep links in Slack/email alerts (#416); unset → alerts omit the link. |
38	| `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` | seeded dev user | a **minimal** real allowlist — admins can read every suite's failing-row samples (see [Operational notes](#operational-notes)). |
39	| `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | keep **`true`** — the fixed-window throttle on every public surface (REST + webhooks + `/mcp`), ADR 0035. Fail-open (a Redis outage disables it, logged); set `false` only to fully disable. |
40	| `RATE_LIMIT_AUTHENTICATED_PER_MINUTE` / `RATE_LIMIT_UNAUTHENTICATED_PER_MINUTE` / `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_PER_MINUTE` | `300` / `120` / `120` | per-minute caps, keyed per `sha256(bearer)` (authenticated) or client-IP (rest). The webhook cap is **per provider + IP** (#785) — each of adf/airflow/dbt has its own bucket at this cap; the per-IP webhook *total* is `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_IP_PER_MINUTE`. Defaults are generous; **tighten `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_PER_MINUTE`** to your orchestrator's real callback cadence. |
41	| `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK_IP_PER_MINUTE` | `240` | per-IP ceiling across **all** webhook buckets from one IP (#785) — bounds the aggregate a single IP can spend by rotating provider segments; without it, per-provider buckets would multiply the per-IP webhook budget. |
42	| `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_PER_MINUTE` | `10` | strict per-IP cap for `/api/v1/auth/*` (OTP mint/verify, #1127) — checked **before** the bearer branch, so a token can't dodge it. This is the per-IP **backstop**; the tight screw is `AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_PER_EMAIL_PER_10MIN` below. **Tuning note (NAT pools):** per-IP buckets fold onto `RATE_LIMIT_IPV4_PREFIX` (default /24), so an entire corporate-NAT or campus egress range shares these 10 requests/minute — a burst of simultaneous sign-ins from one office can lock the pool out for the window. If your users sign in from behind one egress, **raise this** (30–60 is still a meaningful cap) rather than narrowing the global prefix to /32, which would strip NAT-evasion protection from the `webhook` and `unauth` classes too. The per-email counter is what actually bounds abuse per mailbox, and it is unaffected by NAT. |
43	| `RATE_LIMIT_IP_PER_MINUTE` | `1200` | per-IP ceiling across **all** bearer buckets from one IP — the rotated-token backstop (a client cycling a fresh random `Bearer` per request can't mint unlimited fresh per-token buckets to dodge the cap). Applies only to the `default` (bearer) class; the unauth class is already per-IP, the webhook class has its own ceiling above. |
44	| `RATE_LIMIT_IPV4_PREFIX` / `RATE_LIMIT_IPV6_PREFIX` | `24` / `64` | per-IP buckets key on this address **prefix**, not the full address (#789) — a rotating NAT/proxy pool inside one allocation shares a bucket instead of diluting the cap across sibling /32s. `/32` / `/128` disable grouping; widen or narrow per deployment (a CGNAT-heavy user base may warrant `/32`). |
45	| `RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS` | `1` | number of trusted proxies that append `X-Forwarded-For` in your deployment — the real client is the entry that many hops from the right. **`1`** for a single-proxy / compose setup (rightmost); **`3`** for the ACA public-envoy→nginx→internal-envoy chain (set in the IaC stack). A chain shorter than this falls back to the socket peer. |
46	| `AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST` / `_PORT` / `_USERNAME` / `_FROM` / `_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME` | unset | email OTP sign-in (ADR 0032) — the third authenticator, for deployments with **no IdP**. Set all four (port defaults to 587) to enable the mailer; the password resolves from the SecretStore **by name**. Deliberately separate from the `EMAIL_*` alert mailer, so a misconfigured alert channel can never block sign-in. **A partial block refuses to boot**, naming the missing vars. **Verify it actually works** with the admin SMTP pre-flight test (#737) — `POST /api/v1/admin/auth-email/test` as a workspace admin sends a real message to the caller's own address and, on failure, names the exact transport stage that broke (`connect` / `tls` / `auth` / `send`) in the error envelope's `detail.stage` — catches a misconfigured relay at install time instead of at a teammate's first sign-in attempt. **`/mcp` stays mounted in this mode** (#1128) — but with no IdP there is no bearer token to validate, so a **PAT (`dq_live_…`) is the only credential it accepts**: raw JWTs and session cookies are both rejected. Tell MCP users to mint an API key. |
47	| `AUTH_EMAIL_TLS_MODE` | `starttls` | the OTP mailer's SMTP transport ([#1146](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1146)) — `starttls` (default, unchanged: connect in the clear on 587, then upgrade) / **`implicit`** for a submission relay on **:465** (SMTPS — the socket is TLS from the first byte, so `starttls` would fail against it) / **`none`**, a deliberate PLAINTEXT downgrade for a loopback/same-host relay or a throwaway test rig ONLY — the code and the SMTP password cross the wire unencrypted, and every send logs a loud `otp_smtp_tls_disabled` warning naming it. There is deliberately **no** verify-off/insecure-skip option alongside this: `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE` below covers the legitimate "my relay's cert isn't publicly trusted" case, and weakening certificate verification was rejected as a shortcut around it. |
48	| `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE` | unset | a PEM path of CA certificate(s) the OTP mailer's SMTP connection trusts **instead of** the system store — for an internal relay signed by a private CA ([#1146](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1146)). Scoped to the mailer's own per-send `SSLContext` only — it never touches the process-wide trust store, which is exactly the footgun this replaces: before this option, the only way to reach a private-CA relay was `SSL_CERT_FILE` on the whole api/worker process, silently reconfiguring every OTHER TLS client too (Key Vault, Snowflake, ADLS, webhooks). A path that doesn't name an existing file **refuses to boot**, naming it — the same fail-at-startup discipline as the mailer block above, not a `FileNotFoundError` on the next sign-in attempt. |
49	| `ADMIN_EMAIL_PREFLIGHT_PER_10MIN` | `3` | per-**admin** cap on `POST /api/v1/admin/auth-email/test`, 10-minute window ([#1147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1147)). Every call opens a **real SMTP connection to your relay**, and the endpoint otherwise sits in the generic `RATE_LIMIT_AUTHENTICATED_PER_MINUTE` class (300/min per token) that was sized for ordinary API traffic — a scripted or compromised admin token could burn hundreds of connections a minute and get your **sending account throttled or blocked by the relay**, which takes the real sign-in mailer down with it. Over the cap is a plain `429` (`preflight_rate_limited`, `detail.retry_after_seconds`) — there is no anti-enumeration reason to soften it, the caller is a known admin. Uses the **same counter store** as `AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_PER_EMAIL_PER_10MIN` but a **separate key space**, so the two budgets never consume each other; keyed on a digest of the admin's user id, never their address. Counts **before** the send, so a failed attempt still spends a slot. Fails **open** if the counter store is down. **`0` disables the cap** — the endpoint falls back to the 300/min class, re-accepting the #1147 risk in full. |
50	| `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS` / `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` | unset | **mandatory** signup allowlist — there is no open registration (DataQ holds failing-row samples, which are PII). At least one entry is required whenever the mailer block is set, or the app refuses to boot. Bootstrap: put your own address in this list **and** `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`. |
51	| `AUTH_SESSION_TTL_HOURS` | `24` | session cookie lifetime — a fixed horizon with **no refresh token**; re-running the OTP flow is the refresh. Expiry and logout revocation are enforced on every request. |
52	| `AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` | unset (inferred) | when unset, `Secure` is inferred from `X-Forwarded-Proto` — only trustworthy if the proxy forwards the **real** client-facing scheme. The reference frontend nginx now does: it forwards the **edge's** header and falls back to its own `$scheme` only when there is none (direct connection) — [#1138](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1138); before that fix it overwrote the header with its own plaintext upstream scheme and the cookie shipped **without** `Secure` over HTTPS. Behind your **own** proxy, verify the forwarding — or set this to `true` explicitly, which is valid belt-and-braces on any HTTPS deployment and stops consulting the header at all. Leave unset only for genuinely plain-HTTP local dev — hard-coding `true` there breaks the cookie *silently* (the browser accepts the `Set-Cookie` and then never sends it back). **Runbook note:** the fix rides the **frontend image**, so an existing deployment picks it up on the next frontend roll; until then, or to be certain, set `AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true` on the api Container App. |
53	| `AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_PER_EMAIL_PER_10MIN` | `3` | per-**mailbox** cap on code requests, 10-minute window (#1127). **Active regardless of `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED`** — dev and E2E disable the middleware, and a mail-bomb control a test harness switches off is not a control. Fails **open** if Redis is down (logged once, never the address). A throttled request returns the same uniform `ok` as a successful one; a 429 would tell an attacker which addresses are allow-listed. |
54	| `AUTH_OTP_REQUEST_MIN_SECONDS` | `1.0` | constant-time **floor** on `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request` ([#1137](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1137)) — every uniform response (sent / ineligible / throttled) is held to this minimum, so the code-mint + SMTP round trip an eligible address pays no longer stands out against an ineligible one's in-memory lookup. Error responses (502/503) are deliberately **not** padded — they are already non-uniform by design (a mail outage is operator-visible, not a per-address secret). Raise it if your relay is routinely slower than a second; **`0` disables the floor — re-opens the #1137 timing channel**. Not a constant-time guarantee: a send slower than the floor still overruns it, bounded by `AUTH_EMAIL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. |
55	| `AUTH_OTP_VERIFY_MIN_SECONDS` | `0.5` | the same **floor** on `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify` ([#1141](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1141)). Every rejected code answers a byte-identical 401, but an address with a **live code outstanding** pays an `UPDATE … RETURNING` + commit that an address with none never pays — and that difference is cheap to set up, because a code is minted **only for an allow-listed address**, so one `otp/request` against the address being probed (uniform `ok` either way, revealing nothing itself) creates it for the price of a per-email quota slot. Every 401 is held to this minimum. A **successful** verification is deliberately **not** padded (a 200 already separates itself, to a caller who by definition knows the code), so real sign-ins stay snappy; neither is the 503 for an unconfigured deployment. Half the request-side floor because there is no SMTP tail to clear — only two DB round trips. **`0` disables it — re-opens the #1141 timing channel.** Same caveat: a DB round trip slower than the floor overruns it. |
56	| **Frontend OTP mode** | `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` | set `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=otp` **together with** the backend block above — these are **two coordinated selectors** (ADR 0032 decision 2) and neither can infer the other. Backend OTP on + frontend on `oidc` ⇒ the SPA shows an OIDC flow against an IdP that is not configured; frontend `otp` + backend off ⇒ the code form 503s. |
57	| `COMPARISON_MAX_ROWS` | `100000` | default per-side row cap for `comparison` checks (ADR 0015) — both sides materialize in worker memory for the diff, so this is a memory guardrail; over-cap runs **fail fast** (never a silently truncated diff). A check's `config.max_rows` overrides it. |
58	| `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` | unset | Azure Monitor / App Insights backend for spans + logs (observability, OTel — ADR 0010). |
59	| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | unset | generic OTLP/HTTP backend for spans + logs (#589) — any OTLP consumer (Tempo/Jaeger/Datadog/Collector); set alongside App Insights for parity, or alone for a non-Azure deploy. |
60	| `OPENLINEAGE_URL` | unset | OpenLineage emission (ADR 0034, #758) — **dark by default**: unset ⇒ zero emission. Point at an OL receiver (Marquez, DataHub's OL endpoint) and every suite run emits START + terminal RunEvents with DQ facets (5s emit timeout, fail-open, no sample rows ever). Advanced transports via the library-owned `OPENLINEAGE__TRANSPORT__*` / `OPENLINEAGE_CONFIG`; `OPENLINEAGE_DISABLED=true` forces dark. |
61	| `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED` | unset (`false`) | **`true`** on the **worker only** to run the daily `refresh_warehouse_lineage` sweep (ADR 0034, #858) — **dark by default** because the Snowflake `ACCOUNT_USAGE` / UC `system.access` views it reads need a grant the connection principal may not hold. Set in `containerapps.tf` (`local.worker_env`). Only the worker runs beat, so setting it on the api does nothing. |
62	| `LINEAGE_PROVIDER` / `MARQUEZ_URL` | unset | **leave unset** unless you run a lineage server. This deployment deliberately does **not** set them (#1086): Marquez is a dev-only compose profile and production is expected to bring its own catalog (ADR 0034). Set them only when pointing at a reachable OL-compatible server. Two failure shapes differ: an unreachable `MARQUEZ_URL` leaves the pull *configured but failing* (fail-soft, logged, pruning deliberately skipped for cross-source safety); **un-setting the provider is now handled** ([#1090](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1090)) — the next daily `refresh_lineage_pull` tick sweeps the orphaned `source='marquez'` edges (logged as `lineage_pull_orphans_purged`; re-configuring re-pulls). A configured-but-broken provider (typo'd name, missing URL) deliberately does NOT purge. |
63	| `LINEAGE_STALE_AFTER_HOURS` | `48` | staleness window for the asset-view lineage-source banner (#1091): a warehouse lineage source last refreshed longer ago than this is flagged **stale**, independent of error/degraded — a refresh loop that silently stops must not render as healthy. `0` disables. |
64	| `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_MAX_SEEDS` | `500` | seed cap for the Snowflake `GET_LINEAGE` per-seed traversal (#892) — the Enterprise-only top tier walks this many enumerated tables (ADR 0040 seam) per refresh, **two round trips each** (upstream + downstream), so it is a latency/cost bound. Overflow walks the first N in catalog order and logs `get_lineage_seeds_truncated`; `<=0` removes the bound. Ignored on Standard accounts (the tier is edition-gated) and by every other tier. |
65	| `ASSET_INVENTORY_MAX_TABLES` | `2000` | per-connection cap on the #919 warehouse inventory sync (ADR 0040 — opt-in per connection via the `inventory_sync` config toggle); overflow syncs the first N in catalog order and logs `inventory_sync_truncated`. `<=0` removes the bound. UC connections need `SELECT` on `system.information_schema` (same grant class as the lineage pull's `system.access`); a sync failing on grants logs `inventory_sync_connection_failed` per tick. |
66	| `POLL_STALENESS_ALERT_AFTER_S` | `1800` | workspace-wide dead-poll alert (#1052), **api-side**: the API lifespan loop alerts the workspace Teams/Slack/email channels when `max(last_polled_at)` over ALL orchestration connections exceeds this age — it fires precisely when the worker is too broken to alert for itself. `0` disables the loop. Set on the **api** (the worker value is ignored — deliberately: the check must not live in the process it monitors). |
67	| `key_vault_purge_protection` (OpenTofu var) | `false` (bring-up) | **`true`** for a hardened vault (irreversible). |
68	| Interactive API docs | served | **404 in prod** via the prod-docs gate (`ENVIRONMENT=prod`). |
69	
70	### 2. Access you need
71	
72	- **Azure subscription** — rights to create the resource group, Container Apps
73	  environment, PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Cache for Redis, Key Vault, and Application
74	  Insights + Log Analytics (Contributor on the RG/subscription); the frontend is a
75	  Container App too (no Static Web App since ADR 0028). **Plus** `User Access
76	  Administrator`/`Owner` to grant the managed identity a **custom get+list+set Key Vault
77	  role** (an RBAC role assignment — read+write so the app can persist/rotate connection
78	  credentials at runtime, but not the broader built-in Secrets Officer; #622).
79	- **Azure AD (Entra ID)** — `Application Administrator` (or Global Admin) to create the
80	  **two app registrations** (API + SPA) and **grant admin consent** for the API scope.
81	- **Subscription resource-provider registration** — the app's OpenTofu stack registers
82	  `Microsoft.App`, `Microsoft.Cache`, `Microsoft.KeyVault`, `Microsoft.Web` (see
83	  [rp.tf](terraform/azure/rp.tf)); the PostgreSQL + monitoring providers
84	  (`Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL`, `Microsoft.Insights`, `Microsoft.OperationalInsights`)
85	  come registered with the shared harness resources (ADR 0024). Registration needs
86	  subscription-level rights.
87	- **GitHub repo admin** — to set the Actions [secrets/vars](#github-config-the-workflow-reads)
88	  and create the OIDC **federated credential** (subject = the repo's `production`
89	  environment). The GHCR image push uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`packages: write`);
90	  the package must be **public** so Container Apps pulls it anonymously (ADR 0023).
91	- **Tooling** — **OpenTofu** (`tofu`; `brew install opentofu`) + the `az` CLI,
92	  authenticated to the subscription. Not Terraform — ADR 0024 amendment (2026-07-27).
93	
94	### 3. Cloud prerequisites
95	
96	DataQ is provider-agnostic by design — Azure is one target behind the app's seams
97	(ADR [0010](../docs/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) /
98	[0013](../docs/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md)), so no cloud is
99	baked into app code. Today **Azure is the supported, implemented target**; AWS and GCP
100	are planned.
101	
102	#### Azure — supported today
103	
104	- An Azure **subscription** + a region with quota for **1 Container Apps environment**,
105	  **1 PostgreSQL Flexible Server**, Cache for Redis, Key Vault, and App Insights + Log
106	  Analytics (the frontend is a Container App, not a Static Web App — ADR 0028).
107	  (Free/trial tiers cap one ACA env + one Postgres
108	  server per subscription, so the app **shares** the RG/env/Postgres server with the
109	  harness and namespaces its own DB + role — ADR [0024](../docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md).)
110	- The **resource providers** and **app registrations** from §2 registered/created.
111	- The **GHCR** backend package public. Then follow [One-time provisioning](#one-time-provisioning).
112	
113	#### AWS — planned (not yet available)
114	
115	Not yet implemented. The seams map to: ECS Fargate or App Runner (api + worker) · RDS
116	for PostgreSQL · ElastiCache for Redis · Secrets Manager (`SecretStore` impl) · CloudWatch
117	+ OpenTelemetry (observability) · Cognito or an OIDC IdP behind `get_current_user`. Track
118	via the anti-lock-in roadmap ([ADR 0013](../docs/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md)).
119	
120	#### GCP — planned (not yet available)
